name: list_clusters
title: List clusters
description: Kubernetes clusters (kubeconfig contexts) the user shared with agents in KubeDrive, with API server and default namespace.

name: list_resource_types
title: List resource types
description: Resource types the cluster serves: type id, kind, whether namespaced. Use the ids with the other tools.

name: list_resources
title: List resources
description: Objects of a type, as kubectl get shows them (server-side columns), one per line.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

name: get_resource
title: Get resource
description: One object as YAML, without managedFields. Secret values are removed; credential-looking fields, env values and strings are masked (best effort).

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

name: get_events
title: Get events
description: Events of one object (type and name), or of a namespace (or all namespaces), newest first.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

type.description: with name: events of that object

name: get_logs
title: Get pod logs
description: The last lines of a pod's container log, with timestamps. Secret-looking values are redacted.

container.description: needed when the pod has several

previous.description: the log of the run before the last restart

name: cluster_problems
title: Cluster problems
description: What needs attention, as KubeDrive's cluster overview shows it: failing pods and workloads, nodes not ready, failed Helm releases, and the last hour's warning events.

name: top
title: Resource usage
description: CPU (millicores) and memory of pods or nodes from metrics-server, busiest first.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

name: check_access
title: Check access
description: Whether the user may do a verb on a type (kubectl auth can-i), by SelfSubjectAccessReview.

verb.description: get, list, watch, create, update, patch, delete…

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

name: diagnose
title: Diagnose object
description: Why an object is unhealthy, by KubeDrive's rules (no AI): each finding with severity, the cause, the evidence (cluster messages, the crashed container's last log lines) and a suggested fix. Types: pods, deployments.apps, statefulsets.apps, daemonsets.apps, replicasets.apps, jobs.batch, services, ingresses.networking.k8s.io, persistentvolumeclaims, nodes. Start here before reading logs and events by hand.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

name: broken_links
title: Broken links
description: Links between objects that lead nowhere, as KubeDrive's map shows them: Ingress rules to a missing Service or port, Services that select no pods, pods that mount or read a ConfigMap, Secret or PVC that does not exist, autoscalers whose target is gone, disruption budgets that match no pods. Optional references are not judged, nor kinds the user may not list.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces (slower on big clusters)

name: upgrade_check
title: Upgrade check
description: What breaks when the cluster moves to a newer Kubernetes minor version (KubeDrive Pro): Helm releases and kubectl-applied manifests that name removed API versions, clients still calling them, kinds removed with no successor, and nodes whose kubelet is too old. Each finding says what to write instead. Read only.

target.description: the minor version of 1.x to check, e.g. 33 for 1.33; default the next one

name: timeline
title: Timeline
description: What changed before it broke: one feed, newest first, of the cluster's events, rollouts (new ReplicaSet revisions with the image that changed), container restarts with exit codes, changes made through KubeDrive with who made them, Helm revisions and firing alerts. With type and name: that object and what it is joined to; without: the whole cluster. Start here for "what happened" and "why did it break". Windows beyond 1h need KubeDrive Pro.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

linked.description: include the objects it is joined to (pods, Services, Ingresses, ConfigMaps, autoscaler); default true

name: rightsizing
title: Rightsizing
description: Compares what the cluster's containers request with what they used, from Prometheus (KubeDrive Pro): workloads at risk (killed for memory, throttled by a CPU limit, no requests, using more than they request) and over-requested ones, each container with current and suggested requests and limits (CPU from the 95th percentile, memory from the highest use, plus the user's headroom). Read only; set resources with the edit tools.

window.description: how far back to look; default 7d

name: apply
title: Apply a manifest
description: Changes an object to match the manifest (kubectl apply on one object): a server-side dry run first, then the user sees the diff in KubeDrive and allows or declines. The manifest is the whole object as get_resource returns it, edited; fields left out are removed.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

name: scale
title: Scale a workload
description: Sets the replicas of a Deployment, StatefulSet or ReplicaSet, after the user allows it in KubeDrive.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

name: restart
title: Restart a workload
description: Rolls out new pods for a Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet (kubectl rollout restart), after the user allows it.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

name: rollback
title: Roll back a workload
description: Returns a Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet to an earlier revision (kubectl rollout undo); without a revision, the previous one. The user allows it in KubeDrive.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

name: delete
title: Delete an object
description: Deletes one object after the user allows it in KubeDrive; namespaces and cluster-scoped objects always need the name typed by the user.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

name: cordon
title: Cordon a node
description: Marks a node unschedulable, after the user allows it.

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

name: uncordon
title: Uncordon a node
description: Marks a node schedulable again, after the user allows it.

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

name: drain
title: Drain a node
description: Cordons a node and evicts its pods (kubectl drain; DaemonSet pods stay), after the user allows it. Pods with emptyDir volumes or without a controller are skipped unless the options say otherwise.

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

force.description: also evict pods no controller will recreate

name: trigger_cronjob
title: Run a CronJob now
description: Creates a Job from a CronJob right away, after the user allows it; returns the Job's name.

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

name: port_forward
title: Open a port forward
description: Forwards a local port on this computer to a pod, service or workload, after the user allows it; returns the local port and the forward's id (port_forward_stop closes it). The forward stays open until stopped or KubeDrive quits.

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

port.description: the port in the pod or service

name: port_forward_stop
title: Close a port forward
description: Closes a port forward opened by port_forward, by its id. No confirmation.

name: exec
title: Run a command in a container
description: Runs one command (an argument list, no shell) in a container without a terminal, after the user allows it: stdout, stderr and the exit code come back, each output cut at 256 KB. Up to 60 seconds.

reason.description: why, in one line; the user sees it with the change

namespace.description: namespace; empty for all namespaces or cluster-scoped types

container.description: needed when the pod has several

command.description: the program and its arguments, e.g. ["nginx","-T"]
